title: Sikhs
capsule: Between 1709 and 1718 Banda Singh Bahadur, a military commander commissioned by Guru Gobind Singh, led the first organized exercise of Sikh political authority in the Punjab. After a decisive victory at the Battle of Sirhind (1710), Banda abolished zamindari land tenure in captured territories and struck coins in the names of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh—unprecedented sovereign assertions. Mughal governor Abd us-Samad Khan systematically reduced Banda's strongholds; Banda was captured at Gurdas Nangal in December 1715 and executed in Delhi in June 1716, and Mughal forces suppressed the broader movement by 1718. This episode prefigured the Sikh Misls of the 1740s and ultimately the Sikh Empire under Ranjit Singh.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The military and political history is documented in Mughal administrative records and Sikh hagiographical sources; the territorial extent of Sikh-controlled areas during 1709–1718 shifted rapidly and cannot be mapped with precision.
